title: Graphics, guns, soldiers and feel
notes: A real sky: physically based scattering, drifting clouds, and light from the sky on everything (metal and plastic now reflect it).

Post-processing: colour grading, vignette, film grain and lens fringing; bloom on muzzle flashes and explosions (High); ambient occlusion for soft contact shadows (new Ultra setting). Being hurt drains the colour and darkens the edges; rounds snapping past smear the edges of your view.

Guns rebuilt with rounded parts and real detail: rail teeth, M-LOK slots, charging handles, ejection ports, forward assists, triggers and guards, ribbed magazines, slide serrations, scope rings, sling swivels.

Soldiers rebuilt: rounded bodies with faces and ears, plate carriers with cummerbunds, loaded magazine pouches, radios, hydration packs, a holstered pistol, cargo pockets, knee pads and proper boots; helmets with rails, NVG mounts and chin straps.
Better animation: legs step the way you are actually moving when strafing or backing up, the body leans into a sprint, hips sway, soldiers breathe when standing still.

The maps are lived in: window frames and sills, painted shutters and open doors, water tanks and satellite dishes on the roofs, AC units on the walls, oil drums, tyres, rubble, dry scrub, rubbish, better palm trees; at the port, jersey barriers, pallet stacks, cable reels, puddles and lane markings.
Effects: a 3D muzzle flash, glowing tracers, chips of plaster, wood and concrete that fly off walls and bounce, and explosions with a fireball, a shockwave ring, flying dirt and a column of smoke.
Feel: recoil kicks and springs back, a short camera punch per shot, the gun rolls as you strafe and dips when you land.
Faster despite all that: whole soldiers, guns and scenery are merged into a few draw calls each. Low and Medium stay light for weaker PCs.

title: Real gunshots
notes: Every gun now fires real recordings (from the CC0 Free Firearm Sound Library): AR-15, AK-47 and SKS, a .30-06 Tikka for the battle rifles, Springfield 1917 and Mosin Nagant for the snipers, three real 12-gauge pump guns, Walther PPQ, Colt 1911, a .38 revolver and a Swedish K submachine gun.
Gunfire far away uses recordings made at a distance, so a firefight across the map sounds like one: duller, with the echo coming back off the buildings.
The .50 BMG and .50 AE use those recordings pitched down. Reloads, impacts and explosions are still synthesized for now.

title: COLD BORE
notes: A realistic online multiplayer FPS: Free-for-all, Team Deathmatch and Domination on two maps (Al-Hadra, a desert town, and Kessel Freight Yard, a container port).
Quick Play finds an online match; if there isn't one, you host one and bots fill the empty places. Bots leave as real players join. Server browser, private matches with a code, and offline vs bots.

27 real guns at their real prices (a Glock 17 is $550, an M4 $1,150, a Barrett M82 $9,500), real attachments (EOTech, ACOG, suppressors with the $200 tax stamp), melee weapons, grenades, first aid and armour. Kills pay $500 (+$250 headshot) and the money is yours for the match.
Ballistics: bullet drop, travel time, penetration through walls and bodies, armour levels IIIA / III / IV and helmets that stop what they would really stop.
Wounds where the rounds land, bleeding you have to treat (bandage, tourniquet, IFAK), limping on a leg hit, shaking aim on an arm hit. Ragdolls. Realistic gore with a slider from 0 (none) to 100.
Your bank (every dollar you earn) buys uniforms and Cerakote finishes in the Armory. Controllers (Xbox, PlayStation, Steam Deck), installable as an app.
